L106@P2: We further define a notion of divisorial stability, where one tests stability through
L107@P2: convex combinations of divisorial valuations on X (which can be encapsulated into
L108@P2: so-called divisorial measures). Our main result proves the following characterisation
L109@P2: in our setting, generalising the work of Boucksom–Jonsson2.
L110@P2: Theorem 1.1. Suppose X is a smooth projective variety, and L is a big line bundle
L111@P2: on X. Then (X, L) is uniformly K-stable if and only if it is divisorially stable.

L172@P4: We end with a more philosophical comment on our approach to uniform Kstability in the big setting, which is motivated by considerations from non-Archimedean
L173@P4: geometry. Boucksom–Jonsson [BJ22] have given a general theory of plurisubharmonic metrics in non-Archimedean geometry, for arbitrary pseudoeffective classes.
L174@P4: Our work is strongly influenced by theirs, but does not use the same approach; our
L175@P4: notion of a test configuration is distinct from their notion of a non-Archimedean
L176@P4: Fubini–Study metric.
L177@P4: More precisely, in the complex (Archimedean) theory, a plurisubharmonic metric
L178@P4: can be viewed as a decreasing limit of (in general singular) Fubini–Study metrics
L179@P4: through Demailly approximation [Dem92], which is taken as a definition in nonArchimedean pluripotential theory. Our approach is instead motivated by the fact
L180@P4: that plurisubharmonic envelopes of continuous functions are dense in the space
L181@P4: of metrics with minimal singularities; our test configurations are analogues of such
L182@P4: plurisubharmonic envelopes. In the Boucksom–Jonsson theory, a major issue is that
L183@P4: the space of finite energy plurisubharmonic non-Archimedean metrics with minimal
L184@P4: singularities is not known to be complete in general, even in the big and nef case
L185@P4: (see [DXZ25] for related results using the formalism of [RN14]). The approach
L186@P4: which we take means we do not require analogous completeness results to obtain a
L187@P4: working theory, such as in our approach to the non-Archimedean Monge–Amp`ere
L188@P4: equation.

L338: We assume throughout this section that $X$ is smooth.
L339: ### 3.1. The Monge–Ampère measure of a test configuration
L340: To a test configuration $(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{L})$, we may associate a divisorial measure $\mu=\{E_{i},\xi_{i}\}$ essentially by letting $E_{i}$ be the components of $\mathcal{X}_{0}$ and letting $\xi_{i}$ be a normalised version of $\langle\mathcal{L}^{n}\rangle\cdot E_{i}$.
L341: Our interest in the present section is the inverse question: given a divisorial measure $\mu$, can we produce a test configuration whose associated measure is $\mu$? Concretely, can we prescribe the restricted volumes of a big line bundle along the central fibre of a test configuration? This question can be phrased through non-Archimedean geometry, where it corresponds to solving a non-Archimedean Calabi–Yau theorem.

L389: Provided one endows $X^{\mathrm{div}}$ with the structure of a topological space, the Monge–Ampère measure can be viewed as a (discrete) measure on $X^{\mathrm{div}}$, simply by defining it to be $\sum_{i}\mathrm{vol}(L)^{-1}(b_{i}\langle\mathcal{L}\rangle^{n}\cdot E_{i})\delta_{E_{i}}$.
